I BROKE THE LIVE SITE for about two minutes. The comment I wrote above the fold-toggle rule sits INSIDE ui/tree/tree.js s css(template) call and quoted three class names in backticks, so the template literal closed early and the whole module was a SyntaxError: every page rendered nothing and the owner saw it. The mastermind stripped the three backticks at 14:54. This is the CLAUDE.md trap word for word - one backtick inside css(template) kills every page - and node --check catches it in one second. From here: node --check after every .js write, then a headless load, before anything else.

assign.now: framework.css mechanism, tree row, filter bar and avatar all written; taking the AFTER shots

decision.chose: The three ground utilities carry the token. .darken-1/-2/-3 in framework.css paint the ground AND set --field-bg; a second rule right after the control box gives input, select and textarea background-color: var(--field-bg, var(--fill-a08)). Buttons are excluded on purpose - a button already has a fill to say what it is.
decision.alternative: A .bar word carrying both the ground and the token. Rejected because a bar is not the only darkened thing on a page (a band, a card, a photo strip all take a darken ground), and a word that means both a ground and a role would have to be re-invented the first time someone wanted the ground without the role. The ground words already existed as tokens with no classes; giving them classes was the smaller change.
decision.cost: --field-bg inherits, so every field anywhere under a darken ground goes to the surface colour, including one inside a nested white card - where it is already right. Nothing moves until an element opts in.

decision.topic: darken-1 or darken-2 for the filter bar
decision.chose: darken-2 (16%). Decided by shooting both at 1920, not by argument.
decision.alternative: darken-1 (8%), the brief first suggestion. At 8% the bar barely read as a band at all, and the white field own 32% hairline was DARKER than the ground it sat on, which inverts the relationship the bar exists to show. At 16% the bar is plainly a bar and the field is the brightest thing on it.

decision.topic: how the filter stops drawing its card
decision.chose: A config word on ux/Filter: chrome: false skips the .surface.pad box, and nothing else changes. Sidebar passes it, and adds .darken-2 in the markup.
decision.alternative: A .sidebar-filter { border: none; background: none; padding: 0 } override from Sidebar.css. Rejected on the framework own rule - overriding a base look is a bug report about the base, not a fix - and because the caller that KNOWS it is nested is the one that should say so. Also removed: the empty segment row Filter drew when segments is empty, which the parent gap then pushed the field 25px to the right of.

decision.topic: should the square icon frame become the site-wide default for .icon
decision.chose: NO, not today - the frame lives on ui/tree rows and on the sidebar footer controls only. framework.css .icon keeps font-size: 1.25em; line-height: 1; flex: 0 0 auto.
decision.alternative: Make .icon itself a square frame (width: 1.4em, aspect-ratio: 1, display: grid, place-items: center). It is the RIGHT default and should be proposed properly: icon() is called from 300 call sites across 131 files, and .icon today has no width at all, so it is as wide as whatever glyph it holds. Giving it a fixed square would re-space every one of those rows at once - a tab strip, a button with a leading icon, a crumb, a table cell - and some of them are already compensating with their own margins. That is a site-wide visual change and its own task with its own before/after sweep, not a side effect of fixing a rail.
decision.needs: the owner call, plus a shot sweep of the biggest icon consumers (tabs, buttons, crumbs, page previews) before and after

log.msg: The icon frame measured. --ui-tree-frame: 1.3em is declared on .ui-tree-row and both the fold and the icon read it, with display: grid, place-items: center, aspect-ratio: 1 and line-height: 1. At 1920 both boxes are exactly 16.63px square and the icon GLYPH INK centre is 0.07-0.08px from the label ink centre on five rows out of five (the box centres were already identical; it was line-height 1.4 sitting the glyph on its own baseline that made it ride high). ⚠ Found while doing it: an em inside an UNREGISTERED custom property is not resolved where it is declared - it inherits as a token stream and resolves at the element that USES it. While the fold still carried font-size 0.9em, the one token made a 16.63px icon box and a 14.97px fold box. Dropping the fold font-size override is what made one token mean one number.

The footer white block, cause in one sentence: .sidebar-rail declared max-height: 100dvh and no height, and max-height only CAPS a box rather than filling one, so the rail was exactly as tall as its content and on a short tree (the home page, nine rows) the footer stopped where the last row stopped with the rest of the rail left blank below it. height: 100dvh above 52em (height: auto below it, or the open menu would be a full-screen sheet) pins the footer and hands the slack to .sidebar-nav, which already had flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto. Measured at 1920x1080: footer 47.1px -> 34.3px, whiteBelowFooter 0, nav scrolls when every branch is opened (1169 rows) and does not when 29 fit. At 3440: 58.6px -> 38.4px.

FORENSICS on the three earlier sidebar tasks. site-sidebar-tree (2026-09-18) kept NO screenshot in its task dir and claimed an 80/80 page crawl, nav-stability across five page switches at 1280/1920/3440 with sidebar x, width and first-five-row y all 0px change, and before/after shots saved to a scratchpad that is gone - every one of those checks is about POSITION and WIDTH, never about what a row looks like. sidebar-filter kept one 170px crop showing the filter and two rows, which is too small a frame to show that the filter was a card inside a rail. tree-fixes kept no screenshot and verified BEHAVIOUR (leaf-awareness, drag-then-click, closed-branch counts) plus row COUNTS matching before and after, and its final sweep line says screenshots 77-178KB each confirming real rendered content - that is a check that something rendered, not that it looked right. No critic pass ran on any of the three. Nobody ever measured a row height, a label x, or the fold glyph, so nobody was in a position to think the rail was acceptable or not.

assign.outcome:
**The rail reads like a file tree again — 46.5px rows to 31.7px, and the filter is a UI bar with a white field.**

[Before and after, at 1280 / 1920 / 3440 and the 400 menu](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/sidebar-repair/)

![the rail after](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/sidebar-repair/shots/after/page-1920.png)

At 1920 — **row pitch 46.5 -> 31.7px** (GitHub's file tree is 32), **label x 80 -> 57.5px** at depth 0 and **80 -> 15.4px** on a rail with no folds or icons, **fold glyph 8.96px in a 12.5px box -> 12.8px in a 16.6px square**, **footer 47.1 -> 34.3px and pinned to the bottom**. The icon's ink now sits **0.08px** from its label's centre, five rows out of five.

**What changed, and where it lives**

- **The row** — `core/Sidebar/Sidebar.css`. Every length the row's own `em`; the old `gap: 1.3em` applied twice is where 25px of dead air between arrow and icon came from. Two `:has()` rules drop the fold and icon columns when no row in a tree uses either, so the home page's nine labels stop floating.
- **One square frame** — `ui/tree/tree.js`. `--ui-tree-frame` on the row, `display: grid; place-items: center; aspect-ratio: 1; line-height: 1` on both children. `line-height: 1` is the half that fixes it: the boxes were already centred, the glyph inside was sitting on its own baseline.
- **Fields on a darkened ground are white** — `framework.css`. `.darken-1/-2/-3` paint the ground AND set `--field-bg`; `input`, `select`, `textarea` read it. Buttons deliberately excluded. [Live example on the design system page](/framework/styles/system/).
- **The filter is a bar** — `ux/Filter` gained `chrome: false` (drops its own card) and stopped drawing an empty segment row; the rail adds `.darken-2` and declares no colour.
- **The footer** — one button row pinned to the bottom. The white block was `.sidebar-rail` declaring `max-height: 100dvh` and no `height`: max-height caps a box, it never fills one.
- **The avatar** holds the anonymous person, two pseudo-elements.

Records: [core/Sidebar/doc/decisions.md](/framework/core/Sidebar/doc/decisions.md) - [ui/tree/doc/decisions.md](/framework/ui/tree/doc/decisions.md) - [ux/Filter/doc/decisions.md](/framework/ux/Filter/doc/decisions.md)

**Left open**

- **The square frame is not `.icon`'s yet.** It should probably be the site-wide default, but `icon()` has 300 call sites in 131 files and `.icon` has no width today, so it would re-space every tab, button and crumb at once. Its own task, with its own sweep. The owner's call.
- **I blanked the live site for about two minutes** writing a comment with backticks inside `ui/tree`'s `css(...)` template. The mastermind fixed it; `node --check` after every `.js` write now, and a line went into the css skill's improvements.
- **Forensics:** none of the three earlier sidebar tasks kept a usable screenshot or ran a critic. They verified position, width, row counts and that something rendered - never what a row looked like.
